transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-15
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Rao (Redwood SE); Marcus Vega (Redwood SE); Amira Patel (CTO, Nova Finance); Diego Morales (Head of InfoSec, Nova); Janelle Park (ML Engineer); Tom Brooks (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping for Nova Finance — focus on security gates (SOC 2 / ISO), SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logging expectations, plus sizing/benchmarks and acceptance criteria for pilot. Goal: pilot in dedicated private deployment (VPC) with encryption at rest, KMS integration, and throughput > 200 reqs/min for small chat completions.

Topics:
- Compliance docs (SOC2, ISO-27001) and timing
- SSO/SAML integration and RBAC provisioning
- Audit logs, retention, and access patterns
- Workload examples, latency/throughput targets, and benchmark plan
- Timeline and success criteria for POC

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh — appreciate you carving time today. quick roll call?
[00:08] Amira Patel: hi, yes Amira here, CTO.
[00:11] Diego Morales: Diego, head of InfoSec.
[00:13] Janelle Park: Janelle, ML eng.
[00:15] Tom Brooks: Tom from procurement.
[00:17] Priya Rao: Priya, Redwood SE, thanks. Marcus here as well.
[00:20] Liam Chen: perfect, so agenda — we'll run through compliance questions first since Diego flagged those, then sizing / benchmarks, then acceptance criteria and next steps. sound good?
[00:27] Diego Morales: yep please start with the compliance list. we have a vendor security review next week.
[00:31] Liam Chen: cool. high level: Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO-27001 summary. we'll attach redacted copies. for private deployments we support customer-managed KMS and HSM via our integrations, encryption at rest in the VPC, and network isolation.
[00:46] Diego Morales: when you say "redacted copies" — will they include the control mappings for data retention and logging? our auditor asks for the control mappings, at least in redacted form.
[00:55] Priya Rao: yeah, we can provide the SOC2 report plus a control mapping spreadsheet that maps SOC controls to our implementation. note that some of the private deployment artifacts are in the private repo but we can export the compliance pack.
[01:07] Diego Morales: okay. what about ISO cert dates and scope — we need to know if infra regions in eu-west are covered.
[01:13] Liam Chen: ISO summary includes regions. eu-west is covered for our hosted control plane and we have private deployment options that can be scoped to your region — we can call out exact scope in the doc we send.
[01:24] Amira Patel: critical for us is SSO and SAML — we need SSO with attribute-based RBAC from our IdP (Okta). provisioning via SCIM would be nice. can Redwood map Okta groups to roles in the console?
[01:36] Marcus Vega: yes — we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. you can map IdP group attributes to Redwood roles, and we support custom role definitions. small caveat: some advanced auditing flags are only available in enterprise license but the POC includes audit logs export.
[01:50] Diego Morales: by "audit logs export" do you mean we get full request/response payloads or just metadata? data exfil concern.
[01:55] Priya Rao: good question. for hosted by default we capture metadata (request id, model, prompt hash, timestamps, user id) and the content of requests is masked. for dedicated/private deployments we can enable detailed logs but we typically recommend storing full raw logs in your own S3 bucket with server-side encryption and our logging agent pushing them. raw payload storage is an opt-in and we can put filters to redact PII.
[02:19] Diego Morales: okay, so for this POC we need to ensure no raw prompts leave our environment. We want the inference to run inside our VPC (private deployment) with no outbound access aside from monitoring and the logging agent to our s3.
[02:30] Priya Rao: that matches what we do for on-prem / VPC installs. we can run in an air-gapped style: inference nodes have no internet egress, the control plane can be customer-hosted or a thin control plane in region, and logs go to customer-managed S3.
[02:44] Janelle Park: for the benchmark, our crown jewel is a customer chat summarization flow — average prompt length ~350 tokens, response ~450 tokens. target p95 latency under 700ms and sustained throughput 200 requests per minute. is that achievable?
[02:57] Priya Rao: depends on model and instance class — with a quantized 70B variant on A100-equivalent or a multi-GPU pooled setup we can plausibly hit those numbers with continuous batching. we should run an initial benchmark with your sample prompts to confirm.
[03:12] Liam Chen: quick note: batching increases throughput but may add 40–100ms depending on buffer window. we can tune for lower latency at cost of unit CPI.
[03:20] Tom Brooks: from procurement perspective, timeline — we want pilot to start by first week of February, run 6 weeks, then decide on dedicated commit. is that realistic?
[03:29] Liam Chen: timeline tight but doable. target start 2027-02-03 for a 6-week pilot. main blockers are security review and sample payload delivery.
[03:37] Amira Patel: acceptance criteria from our side: 1) SOC2 + ISO docs reviewed, 2) SSO with Okta + SCIM working, 3) logs exported to our S3 w/ AES-256 & KMS integration, 4) p95 latency < 700ms on our test set, 5) throughput >= 200 reqs/min for sustained 10-minute window.
[03:54] Priya Rao: got it. we'll include a benchmark plan that measures p50/p95/p99, token cost, and tail latencies. we'll also include a suggested instance mix for the pilot and how to scale.
[04:06] Diego Morales: what about data retention and delete workflows — if a user asks to delete PII, what is the path?
[04:12] Marcus Vega: for private deployments, Redwood can run deletion workflows against customer-managed storage and we provide APIs for record-level purge. for hosted, we retain logs per policy and can support deletion requests mapped to audit ids.
[04:23] Janelle Park: also curious about model pinning and rollbacks — we need deterministic outputs for evaluation. can we pin a model hash and have a reproducible serving image?
[04:32] Priya Rao: yes, you can pin a specific model build, and we keep KV cache compat checks. rollbacks are supported — we include model version in audit logs. small note: when you move between quantization profiles there can be minor output variance.
[04:45] Amira Patel: Diego: do we have any special regulatory requirements for this pilot?
[04:48] Diego Morales: we need data residency in eu and audit trail for all admin actions. also, SSO sessions must have MFA enforced.
[04:55] Liam Chen: MFA enforced via Okta policy is fine — Redwood defers to IdP enforcement for sessions. we can capture admin actions in the audit log and push to your SIEM.
[05:04] Tom Brooks: on pricing/procurement — we'll need a trial pricing sheet and a short-term commitment quote for the pilot. can you provide that?
[05:10] Liam Chen: yes, we'll send a pilot quote and include options: hosted trial vs dedicated-private pilot. since you prefer VPC and no egress, the private pilot option will have a modest deployment fee plus per-hour node pricing.
[05:21] Amira Patel: regarding SAML — we've had issues in past where group attributes didn't sync cleanly; what's the fastest way to test SSO for the POC?
[05:28] Marcus Vega: we usually spin up a test tenant and add a single IdP connection. SCIM can be enabled in test mode to push groups. for the pilot, we recommend a staging Okta app and 2-3 test users to validate role mapping.
[05:38] Diego Morales: audit retention length? we need at least 12 months of admin action logs accessible and 6 months of request metadata.
[05:45] Priya Rao: we default to 12 months for audit logs for enterprise plans; request metadata retention can be configured. for private installs, retention is under your control with S3 lifecycle.
[05:54] Janelle Park: about benchmark methodology, can you walk through what you'll measure?
[05:58] Priya Rao: sure. plan: run your payloads across the candidate model variants (we'll propose 2-3) for a set of concurrency points (1, 5, 20) and measure p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1k tokens. we'll also run a 10-minute sustained load test at target concurrency to confirm throughput.
[06:18] Janelle Park: that sounds right. also would appreciate a reproducible script/terraform to bring up the pilot infra.
[06:24] Marcus Vega: yep, we'll provide terraform snippets and an infra runbook.
[06:28] Diego Morales: a question on KMS — do you support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS and also HSM-backed keys?
[06:34] Priya Rao: yes for private deployments: AWS KMS customer-managed keys supported. HSM integrations are available for enterprise plans; for the pilot we can validate with CMKs.
[06:42] Liam Chen: quick call out on telemetry: we can provide token-level cost breakdowns and sampling of examples for quality monitoring while keeping raw prompts in your S3.
[06:52] Amira Patel: regarding acceptance — will Redwood provide a final report at end of pilot with measurements and recommendations?
[06:57] Liam Chen: yes, final pilot report with benchmark results, cost estimates, and recommended production sizing.
[07:03] Tom Brooks: okay next steps recap?
[07:06] Liam Chen: quick recap: 1) Redwood sends SOC2 & ISO summary + control mapping (by 2027-01-20) 2) Nova to upload sample workload and 3 example prompt classes (by 2027-01-18) 3) Redwood drafts benchmark plan and infra terraform snippets (by 2027-01-22) 4) Schedule hands-on sizing workshop week of 2027-01-25 5) Procurement to receive pilot quote (by 2027-01-19).
[07:26] Tom Brooks: sounds good. Diego, any blockers on security side?
[07:29] Diego Morales: just want to review SOC2 mapping before approval. also will need contact for our legal team.
[07:35] Liam Chen: Liam's on point for SOC2; Marcus will be technical contact; Marcus send contact details after the call.
[07:41] Janelle Park: small note — I'll include a folder with the prompt variations and the summarization rubric.
[07:45] Amira Patel: thanks, everyone. quick aside — are you planning to support FedRAMP or other regional compliances? not urgent for this pilot but curious.
[07:53] Priya Rao: we do not currently have FedRAMP but we have roadmap items for additional compliance in 2027. we'll share the roadmap doc.
[07:59] Liam Chen: cool, any other questions?
[08:02] Diego Morales: none from me.
[08:04] Tom Brooks: no.
[08:05] Liam Chen: alright we'll follow up via email with the docs and calendar invites. thanks all.

Notes on transcription: some words may be mistranscribed (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "Sam L" for SAML), filler words left in; speakers sometimes overlap.
